passage: The rain had turned the pitch to mud, and the final was in forty minutes. Coach Ujjwal read out the starting eleven, and Parveen's name wasn't in it again. She stared at her boots. He always picks Kavya and Nisha, she thought. She wanted to throw her bib down and walk out. But her bus fare was already paid and her mother was coming to watch. Instead, at the interval she went to him. "Coach, what do I need to fix to start?" He looked surprised. "Your first touch under pressure. You panic when the ball arrives." She nodded. "Then I'll stay after practice." Her jaw still felt tight when she came on for the last ten minutes, but she had something to work on.

qa.q: How long before the final was the starting eleven read out?
What did Parveen think and want when her name wasn't in the starting eleven?
qa.a: She thought Coach Ujjwal always picks Kavya and Nisha, and she felt hurt enough to want to throw her bib down and walk out.

qa.q: What small step helped Parveen after being benched?
qa.a: She asked the coach directly what she needed to fix and then planned to stay after practice, instead of quitting angrily or complaining behind his back.

qa.q: How might Coach Ujjwal have felt when Parveen asked her question?
qa.a: Surprised, as his face showed, and probably pleased that she asked. He gave her a specific, honest answer about her first touch.

grounding: A benched player resents the coach but asks what to improve and keeps training instead of quitting or gossiping.

passage:
Tuesday
Benched again. Third match in a row. Coach Mridul put Sakshi in my position even though I scored twice in the last practice game. I sat on the bench with my knees up, boiling.
In the changing room, some girls were talking about how Coach has favourites. I nearly joined in. I also nearly told him I'm quitting, right there, just to see his face.
I didn't. I cried on the walk home instead.
Tonight I thought about it more calmly. Maybe he does prefer Sakshi. Or maybe there's something I'm not seeing.
So tomorrow before practice I'm going to ask him, "Sir, what do I need to improve to get back in the team?" If he gives me something real, I'll work on it. If he doesn't, at least I'll know.
And I'm still going to training. Quitting in a temper would just prove I'm not ready.
Avni

qa.q: Who did Coach Mridul put in Avni's position?
What was Avni feeling on the bench?
qa.a: Avni felt furious and resentful, suspecting Coach Mridul had favourites.

qa.q: What is Avni planning, and why is it wise?
qa.a: To ask the coach directly what to improve and keep training, instead of gossiping or quitting in anger.

qa.q: How might Coach Mridul see Avni's question?
qa.a: He may appreciate the question, seeing it as maturity and commitment rather than a complaint.

grounding: A teen who resents being benched decides to ask the coach what to improve and keep training instead of quitting or gossiping.
